Nephrotic syndrome: 1

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

An adult has generalized edema, heavy urinary protein loss, low serum albumin and elevated lipids. Which syndrome best unifies these findings before a biopsy or other investigation establishes the specific underlying glomerular cause?

  1. Increased circulating lipids
  2. Increased infection susceptibility
  3. Nephrotic syndrome
  4. Reduced plasma oncotic pressure
  5. Hypercoagulability
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Nephrotic syndrome

Heavy proteinuria with hypoalbuminemia and edema defines the core nephrotic pattern, often with hyperlipidemia.

Understanding the options

Nephrotic syndrome
Heavy proteinuria with hypoalbuminemia and edema defines the core nephrotic pattern, often with hyperlipidemia.
Reduced plasma oncotic pressure
Urinary albumin loss contributes to edema; renal sodium retention also matters. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Hypercoagulability
Urinary loss of anticoagulant proteins and other changes increase venous thrombosis risk. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Increased circulating lipids
Nephrotic syndrome can alter lipoprotein synthesis and clearance, producing hyperlipidemia. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Increased infection susceptibility
Loss of immune proteins and some treatments increase infection risk in nephrotic patients. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
